children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children that you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?** If yes, could you please tell me:
- How many children you have
- Their names (or you can use Child 1, Child 2, etc. if you prefer)
- Their ages

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex. I'm not entirely sure of the exact age at the moment, but they're a teenager, somewhere between 15 and 19. We live together here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know that Alex is a teenager between 15 and 19 and lives with you in the UK.

Since Alex's exact age matters for eligibility (there are different rules at 16), I need to narrow this down a bit more:

**Is Alex currently 16 or over, or are they still under 16?**

This is important because:
- If Alex is under 16, you would normally qualify for Child Benefit
- If Alex is 16 or over (but under 20), they would need to be in approved education or training for you to continue receiving Child Benefit

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm honestly not certain whether Alex is over or under 16 right now. I know they're in that teenage range, but I can't give you the exact age at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - without knowing Alex's exact age, this does make it difficult to provide a definitive answer about your eligibility.

Let me ask a different question that might help:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?** (For example, attending school, college, or an approved training course?)

This information is important because:
- If Alex is under 16, you'd normally qualify regardless of education status
- If Alex is 16-19, being in approved education or training is a requirement for you to receive Child Benefit

Even if you're not sure of the exact age, knowing about their education status will help me understand your situation better.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in full-time education at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful, thank you! 

So to summarize what I know so far:
- You have one child, Alex, who is a teenager (between 15-19 years old)
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- Alex is currently in full-time education

Now I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK yourself?** (You mentioned "we live together here in the UK" but I want to confirm your residency status as well)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. We're both here together.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your specific circumstances:

**Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex?** In other words:
- Do you live with Alex day-to-day, OR
- Are you paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards Alex's upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?

Also, **is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm the one responsible for Alex - they live with me day-to-day. And no, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

Just a few more questions to make sure I have the complete picture:

1. **Do you have the right to reside in the UK?** For example:
   - Are you a UK citizen?
   - Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Do you have pre-settled status?
   - Or another immigration status?

2. **Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week?**

3. **Is Alex claiming any benefits in their own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
1. Yes, I have the right to reside in the UK - I'm a UK citizen.

2. No, Alex hasn't started any paid work.

3. No, Alex isn't claiming any benefits in their own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in residential accommodation?** (This would only affect your eligibility if they've been there for more than 8-12 weeks depending on the situation)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in hospital, in care, or in residential accommodation. They're just at home with me.

Thank you for answering all my questions. Let me carefully review your situation:

**Your circumstances:**
- You are a UK citizen living in the UK
- You have one child, Alex, who is a teenager (aged between 15-19)
- Alex lives with you day-to-day
- Alex is in full-time education
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- Alex is not claiming benefits in their own right
- Alex is not in hospital, care, or residential accommodation
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**My assessment:**

Based on the information provided, you appear to meet the basic requirements for Child Benefit. You're responsible for Alex, you both live in the UK, and you have the right to reside here.

However, there is one critical piece of information missing that prevents me from making a definitive determination: **Alex's exact age or whether they are under or over 16**.

Here's why this matters:
- **If Alex is under 16**: You would be **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit
- **If Alex is 16 or over**: The fact that Alex is in full-time education means you would likely be **ELIGIBLE**, BUT I would need to confirm that the education is "approved education or training" as defined by the rules (and that Alex is under 20)

Since you've indicated you cannot confirm Alex's exact age or whether they are over/under 16 at this time, I cannot make a definitive eligibility determination.

Your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex is **INDETERMINATE** at this time because you don't have sufficient information about Alex's exact age.

You can contact the Child Benefit Office directly if you need help confirming your eligibility or have questions about applying. Based on what you've told me, you appear to meet all the other requirements!
